## QUESTION 1

__Write an SQL query that pulls in the the salaries table and the collegeplaying table (and any other tables you might need) and store them in polars dataframes. In Python Polars, combine the dataframes to create a list of baseball players who attended BYU-Idaho. The new table should contain five columns: playerID, schoolID, salary, yearID and teamID associated with each salary.__

The table includes all players who attended BYU-I.

```{python}
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
import sqlite3

sqlite_file = 'lahmansbaseballdb.sqlite'
con = sqlite3.connect(sqlite_file)

salaries = """
  SELECT *
  FROM salaries
  """

dfsalaries = pl.read_database(salaries, con)

collegeplaying = """
  SELECT *
  FROM collegeplaying
  """

dfcollegeplaying = pl.read_database(collegeplaying, con)

result = (dfsalaries
  .join(dfcollegeplaying, on="playerID")
  .select("playerID", "schoolID", "salary", "yearID", "teamID")
  .filter(pl.col("schoolID") == "idbyuid")
)

result
```


## QUESTION 2

1. Pick any two baseball teams and compare them using a metric of your choice (average salary, home runs, number of wins, etc). Be creative! Write a SQL query to read in the table(s) you need, then use polars to manipulate the data. Finally, make a graph using Lets-Plot to visualize the comparison. What do you learn?

This table plots the cumulative number of players for the Atlanta Braves and the Detroit Tigers  who have been inducted into the Hall of Fame. From the graph you can clearly see that the Detroit Tigers have always had more players who have ever been in the hall of fame than the Atlanta Braves. The Detroit Tigers had their first Hall of Fame player in 1936 while the Atlanta Braves only got their first Hall of Fame player in 1978.

During this I learned how to plot cumulative values across a plot which is a bit difficult because you have to manipulate the data a bit more.

```{python}
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
import sqlite3
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)
 
sqlite_file = 'lahmansbaseballdb.sqlite'
con = sqlite3.connect(sqlite_file)

halloffame = """
  SELECT playerID,
         inducted,
         yearid AS yearID
  FROM halloffame
  """

dfhalloffame = pl.read_database(halloffame, con)

appearances = """
  SELECT playerID, 
         teamID
  FROM appearances
  """

dfappearances = pl.read_database(appearances, con)

results = (dfhalloffame
  .join(dfappearances, on="playerID", how="inner")
  .filter(pl.col("inducted") == "Y")
  .group_by(["teamID", "yearID"]).agg(pl.col("playerID").n_unique().alias("hofp"))
  )

cumulative_results = (results
  .filter(pl.col("teamID").is_in(["ATL", "DET"]))
  .sort(["teamID", "yearID"])
  .with_columns(
    pl.col("hofp")
      .cum_sum()
      .over("teamID")
      .alias("cumulative_total")
  )
)

(ggplot(
  cumulative_results.to_dict(as_series = False),
    aes(x = "yearID", y = "cumulative_total", color = "teamID")
    ) + 
    geom_line() + 
    scale_x_continuous(format = "d") +
    labs(
      title = "Cumulative Hall of Fame Players",
      subtitle = "Comparing the Atlanta Braves and Detroit Tigers",
      x = "Year",
      y = "Hall of Fame Players",
      color = "Team"
    )
)
```
